plans.note: No standalone limitation-of-liability heading appears, but the outline skips sections 3, 4, 6, 9 and 11, so a cap may sit in an unextracted clause; check sec-12 (Indemnity) and sec-8 for any embedded liability language. If none exists, we should add a mutual cap with carve-outs.

Section 12 is the indemnity provision; confirm TrueLink (as host/licensor) indemnifies us for third-party IP infringement and its own misconduct, and that our reciprocal indemnity is narrow. Cross-check sec-8 (Client covenants/warranties) for an over-broad Client indemnity trigger.

Restrictions on our business would most likely appear as a Client covenant in sec-8 or as a use limitation in the licence grant (sec-2). Flag only if an actual competitive restraint on Mortgage Logic.com is present.
Hosting/licensing deals often make the Client take Hosting Services solely from the host; review sec-2 (License) and sec-8 (Client covenants) for sole-source or exclusive-provider wording.
No pricing-parity heading visible; MFN language, if any, would sit in sec-5 (Compensation) or as a Client covenant in sec-8. Treat as absent unless a best-terms undertaking by us appears there.

No non-solicitation heading in the outline; such a covenant would most plausibly be tucked into sec-8 (Client covenants) or near the confidentiality obligations in sec-10. Verify before concluding it is absent.

No term/termination section is present in the extracted outline (numbers 3, 4, 6, 9 and 11 are missing), so termination rights are probably in an unsupplied clause; request the full text before proposing a customer termination-for-convenience right.
No term/renewal heading appears; auto-renewal and notice-window terms would live in the missing term section. Cannot map to a supplied section.
No general/miscellaneous or governing-law section is in the outline; likely in an unextracted trailing clause. Flag for follow-up rather than redline.

Assignment and change-of-control provisions would normally sit in a miscellaneous section that is not among the supplied ids; check the preamble/signature area (sec-preamble, sec-p0002) only for party identification.

Ownership issues will turn on the licence grant in sec-2 and the definitions in sec-1 (Client, Hosting Services); confirm we retain ownership of our content, customer data and any hosted deliverables, and that sec-10 does not treat our data as TrueLink's information.
Section 2 is the licence grant; test scope against the playbook — affiliates and contractors covered, non-revocable at will, and no hidden field-of-use limits imported from the sec-1 definitions.
No audit heading; a usage-verification right would most likely appear as a Client covenant in sec-8 or alongside fee reporting in sec-5. Confirm absence against the unextracted sections.

Check sec-5 (Compensation) for penalties or fixed damages payable by us and sec-7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail) for any per-message or stipulated-damages charge, which would be a liquidated-damages exposure we resist.

Section 8 gives only Client covenants and warranties; the outline shows no corresponding TrueLink performance warranty, so we should seek a reciprocal warranty (with a real remedy) and check the missing sections for service-level language.
No insurance heading appears even though TrueLink hosts our site and data; propose adding standard coverage requirements, referencing sec-12 (Indemnity) as the natural companion clause.
Any minimum fee, guaranteed volume or take-or-pay commitment would be in sec-5 (Compensation), with possible volume caps in the sec-2 licence scope; confirm we have an exit if minimums exist.

No post-termination transition or data-return clause is visible; the closest hook is the confidentiality return-of-materials concept in sec-10. Recommend adding migration assistance and return of our hosted data on exit.
